item.title: Digest for 2026-11-12
item.description:
Your stack

Python 3.14

  • Free-Threaded Python: Why Python Devs Should Know About the ABI — the Real Python podcast covers free-threaded CPython's ABI implications, useful background as 3.14/3.15 lean further into no-GIL builds.

httpx

  • Python HTTPX: Making HTTP Requests With HTTPX2 — covers the HTTPX2 client: async calls, timeouts, streaming, HTTP/2.

AWS Lambda

  • Lambda MicroVMs now support x86 — run x86 workloads under MicroVMs without recompiling.
  • Lambda durable functions gets higher default quotas — raised execution and API rate limits if you've hit throttling.

Step Functions

  • How Zillow runs 100 million daily notifications on Step Functions — replaced 10+ campaign generators with short-lived Express workflows, a solid reference for high-volume fan-out.

Amazon Bedrock

  • Web Search API on Bedrock AgentCore — your code can search the web with one signed call, no gateway needed.
  • OpenAI Codex on Amazon Bedrock — covers access, governance, and cost for running Codex via Bedrock.

Terraform

  • Migrate Sentinel and OPA policies to Terraform policy faster — a new Terraform policy agent converts existing policies automatically.
  • Terraform + IBM Concert for infrastructure risk posture — connects Terraform context to policy-driven governance and vulnerability management.

Dependabot and supply chain

  • Security Hub now provides an SBOM inventory — a continuously updated, org-wide view of software packages on your compute.

MCP

  • A more predictable release cycle for MCP — the spec is moving to a steadier cadence after two years of rapid iteration.
  • Exploring file uploads and downloads in MCP — extends MCP beyond tool calls to handle binary file transfer.

Claude

  • Claude Platform release notes — November 9, 2026 — Dreams (research preview) now supports Claude Fable 5.2.

AI-DLC and AI-assisted development practices

  • AWS Emulator and the engineer's job when agents write the code — Werner Vogels on a local AWS emulator written and tested entirely by agents.
  • AI-driven lifecycle management (AI-PDLC) in AWS Quick — six AWS Quick agents take you from scattered customer signals to a validated prototype.
  • Tests as data: ensuring AI-generated code does what we want — Martin Fowler on why tests lose assurance once agents write both production and test code.

Security (AI and cloud)

  • Two CVEs in Amazon mcp-gateway-registry — missing authorization allows privilege escalation to admin, plus a separate SSRF in the registration API; patch if you run the registry.
  • We Built an Agent That Broke All of Our Security Rules — why agents need their own identities, scoped access, and traceability separate from any human's.
  • AntiFox AI pentesting platform linked to AWS secrets theft — an agentic pentesting tool was used to exfiltrate AWS production credentials.
  • AI agents can be backdoored by editing fewer than 10 neurons — Microsoft researchers show a hidden trigger works with no retraining required.

JavaScript and TypeScript

  • Node.js security releases — November 11, 2026 — coordinated fixes across the 22, 24, and 26 LTS lines.

Java

  • Withdrawing the Primitive Patterns Preview Feature — OpenJDK has stopped work on primitive types in patterns/instanceof/switch rather than ship a sixth preview.

IaC and DevOps

  • Consul 2.1.0 — strengthens networking resilience and security, and extends trusted connectivity for agentic applications.
  • Secure AI credentials from discovery to remediation with Vault Radar and Vault — targets the sprawl of AI provider keys across dev workflows.

Source control and GitHub

  • Issue types and fields now available for personal accounts — brings planning capabilities previously limited to orgs to individual developer repos.

AWS

  • Cognito now supports user pool session management — visibility into and control over user sign-in sessions, useful for SSO/MFA enforcement.
  • AWS Network Security Manager now GA in the EU Sovereign Cloud and 31 more regions.
  • EKS Auto Mode now supports security groups for Pods — different workloads on the same node can carry different EC2 security group rules.
  • AWS Cloud WAN now supports Flow Logs — central visibility into IP traffic across your global network.
  • Detecting silent data corruption on SageMaker HyperPod — three checks added to a PyTorch DDP loop catch GPU faults that quietly poison distributed training.

AI and agents

  • Gemini Decisions API — Google joins OpenAI and Jev in the "decision model" category.
  • llm 0.37.2 — Simon Willison's LLM CLI fixes a security issue in how it handles extra-openai-models.yaml.
  • Gemini 4 Carbon explained — Google's new reasoning model: what it is, what it costs, and how to call it from Python.

Security

  • Critical Apache HTTP/2 flaw (CVE-2026-119618) allows RCE — affects mod_http2 in 2.4.55–2.4.70; Wiz says 64% of cloud environments have vulnerable resources.
  • Microsoft patches 1,259 flaws, including an exploited Outlook bug — the Outlook bug may expose NTLMv2 hashes and is already under active exploitation.
  • CVE-2026-118383: use-after-free in MongoDB Server — unauthenticated clients can trigger it via the primary catch-up process; Datadog has detection guidance.
  • Who runs the ransomware group Qilin? — now the most active ransomware affiliate program, 365+ victims claimed in three months.

AI security

  • The Bitter Wall — output quality is flattening against model intelligence, a brick wall away from what you actually want.
  • Over 35,000 Grok-built apps exposed online — most had no sign-in at all, some leaking confidential data and passwords.
  • Railway: stolen customer AI keys led to $740,000 in unauthorized usage — keys stored on the platform were taken in an October breach.

Feeds that failed

  • CISA advisories (https://www.cisa.gov/cybersecurity-advisories/all.xml): malformed XML (mismatched tag)

item.title: Digest for 2026-11-11
item.description:
Your stack

Amazon Bedrock

  • OpenAI's cybersecurity models Daybreak Red and Daybreak Blue are now on the bedrock-runtime endpoint, for vulnerability research and detection engineering.
  • Kimi K3.1 Pro (Moonshot AI) is now on Bedrock via the OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions, Responses and Converse APIs.
  • A worked example shows building a daily dependency watcher with LangGraph and Bedrock AgentCore's Web Search API, signed with your own AWS creds.
  • A new playbook covers evaluating agents on Bedrock AgentCore with built-in, DeepEval and AutoEval checks for task completion and data leaks.
  • Trovata's case study covers autonomous treasury agents on Bedrock and AgentCore, RBAC-secured for bank-branded deployment.
  • TCS describes an agentic test orchestrator on AgentCore that turns requirements into governed tests for regulated clients.
  • A reference architecture for a Bedrock "tokenomics" data lake centralizes invocation logs and cost observability across accounts.

Claude

  • Anthropic's Compliance API now exposes Security posture data in beta for Claude Enterprise orgs.
  • The Anthropic Python SDK shipped 2.8.0; the feed has no changelog detail.
  • Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 launched, with Fable 5.2 reportedly beating GPT-6 Cyber on a cyberattack benchmark.

Claude Code

  • Resend's "Designing for Agents" walks through shaping docs so Claude Code picks the right email API and tools on its own.

MCP

  • zg 0.3.0 moved its local code/doc search pipeline from Node.js to Rust; it's usable from the terminal or through MCP.
  • CVE-2026-125271: the AWS API MCP Server normalized operation names incorrectly, letting requests bypass its security policy checks.

AI-DLC and AI-assisted development practices

  • Gemini 4 Carbon is now GA in GitHub Copilot, for complex coding and agentic tasks.
  • Copilot CLI's C++ language server now auto-configures MSBuild builds, skipping manual compile-command discovery.
  • CVE-2026-124848: Kiro CLI defaulted to overly permissive file permissions on session transcripts/prompt history before 2.27.0 (macOS/Linux).

Source control practices

  • Git 2.56.1 patches six vulnerabilities, including one letting a malicious repo run attacker code via recursive clone.

Dependabot and supply chain

  • From December 8, GitHub will pause Dependabot alerts on repos with no activity in the past year; existing alerts are archived, not deleted.

Security (AI and cloud)

  • CVE-2026-126087: an untrusted search path in OpenJD Sessions for Python hits the launcher behind the AWS Deadline Cloud worker agent.
  • Amazon GuardDuty added options to customize threat-detection features to cut alert fatigue.
  • Wiz reports leaked IAM creds from Qubole's AWS account were used to assume integration roles in customer accounts — worth a cross-account trust check.
  • Fireworks AI's breach investigation widened to include customer datasets, model weights and Notion AI chat data.
  • An RCE flaw in the SGLang inference engine let an attacker run code on a NEAR AI server, exposing data from 18 agents and ~100 users.
  • The Pragmatic Engineer talks with Sean Allen about software correctness and supply-chain security in AI-assisted development.

(Plus today's MCP server, Kiro CLI and Git CVEs above.)

boto3

  • boto3 1.44.0 is out; no changelog detail in the feed.

Powertools for AWS Lambda

  • Powertools for AWS Lambda (Python) shipped 3.40.0; no changelog detail in the feed.

DynamoDB

  • DynamoDB now supports bulk put items, writing data straight from S3 into existing tables.

FastAPI

  • FastAPI shipped two patch releases today, 0.162.3 and 0.162.4; no changelog detail in the feed.

Python

  • Python 3.16.0 alpha 2 is now available for testing.
  • PEP 852 proposes asynchronous functions in the C API.

JavaScript and TypeScript

  • Node.js covers notable V8 changes landing between Node 26 and the Node 27 alpha.
  • JavaScript Weekly's top story: how X (Twitter) rebuilt its web app, replacing three servers with one React/Vite/Fastify app.

Java

  • Spring for Apache Pulsar has a new project home.

IaC and DevOps

  • Platform Engineering Kaigi 2026's recap covers AI-native platform engineering adoption in Japan.
  • Platform Engineering argues agentic development is fragmented while platform engineering as a discipline isn't.

Source control and GitHub

  • GitHub Enterprise Copilot seat management now has GitHub App support.
  • A more informative GitHub dashboard has shipped.

AWS

  • AWS Compute Blog introduces Nitro Sandboxes, hardware isolation for every EKS pod, ECS task and EC2 workload.
  • AWS Network Firewall launches a next-generation firewall policy model with a simpler structure and more rule capacity.
  • Amazon OpenSearch Service now offers managed cross-Region disaster recovery.
  • AWS Architecture Blog shows self-service regional failover with Application Recovery Controller Region Switch and centralized ingress controls.
  • Amazon DocumentDB 8.0.3 adds post-quantum TLS, wildcard indexes and $unionWith.
  • Amazon ElastiCache Serverless now supports vector, full-text and hybrid search with aggregations.

AI and agents

  • Latent Space covers OpenAI discussing new ways of working with Codex at the AI Engineer Code Summit.
  • NaiveAI claims 2,100 tokens/second; Latent Space's hands-on test says its coding quality holds up against DeepSeek.

Security

  • Microsoft's Patch Tuesday fixes nearly 1,100 vulnerabilities across Windows and supported software.
  • SAP patches four CVSS 10.0 flaws, two of them pre-auth remote code execution.
  • N-able took N-central Hosted offline after a researcher disclosed over 30 zero-days with PoC exploits.
  • Chrome patches its eighth actively-exploited zero-day of 2026.
  • Attackers are actively exploiting a critical auth-bypass flaw in Xen Orchestra to gain admin access.
  • Wiz explains how it built a benchmark to evaluate AI agents' offensive cybersecurity capabilities.

Feeds that failed

  • Microsoft Teams Blog (what's new) — malformed XML from techcommunity.microsoft.com.
  • CISA advisories — HTTP 403 Forbidden.

item.title: Digest for 2026-11-10
item.description:
Your stack

  • Linters and type checkers: Astral shipped ty 0.0.100, another point release of its Rust-based Python type checker.
  • boto3: boto3 1.43.127 shipped.
  • DynamoDB: This week's AWS Weekly Roundup highlights AgentCore Runtime V2 and new DynamoDB bulk put items support for writing large batches more efficiently.
  • Amazon Bedrock: AgentCore's Web Search API went GA, giving agents single-call web search without standing up your own MCP tool. AWS also posted a memory-poisoning defense pattern using multi-layer write validation for AgentCore Memory, a seven-layer reference architecture for taking agentic AI to production on AgentCore, and case studies on CrossnoKaye grounding physical AI in live plant data and Novus Hi-Tech's FleetGPT cutting road-behavior violations 46%. Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base also picked up single-shot, retrieval-only requests alongside agentic retrieval.
  • GitHub Actions: GitHub's secret scanning now covers Actions workflow logs (public preview), alongside issues, wikis, discussions and PRs.
  • MCP: Snyk's guide to governing AI coding agents' MCP servers covers inventorying MCP servers, assessing risk and blocking high-risk connections without disrupting developers.
  • Claude: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, both 1M-context, always-on-thinking models (Mythos is restricted to verification-program customers). Fable 5.2 is now the default model in Claude Code 2.1.321 ($8/$40 per Mtok, $0.20/Mtok cache reads) and shipped on AWS and AWS GovCloud, with fast-mode pricing ($16/$80 per Mtok) landing in the Messages API and, per Claude Code 2.1.322, on Vertex. GitHub Copilot also added Fable 5.2. Simon Willison dug into how Fable 5.2 reads prompts about code ownership and added it to llm-anthropic 0.31; anthropic 2.7.0 and claude-agent-sdk 0.2.180 shipped alongside the launch.
  • Security (AI and cloud): AWS flagged two CVEs in the Braket SDK (hybrid-job input download, error-mitigation schema validation) and a path-traversal CVE in ParallelCluster CLI's log-export commands. Datadog's ARTEX writeup shows an AI-native pentesting framework hunting CloudWatch logs and abusing public Cognito pools in the wild, and Wiz traced a breach back to abused IAM credentials from Qubole's own AWS integration.

Python

  • Real Python's guide to TDD with AI agents walks through designing tests first, then letting a coding agent implement against them.

Rust

  • A reader-submitted Nona crypto engine: a #![no_std], zero-heap Rust library for AWS Nitro Enclaves backed by 122 Verus proofs.

Java

  • InfoQ's Java News Roundup covers point releases of TornadoVM, A2A for Java, Gradle and EclipseStore, plus a new Open Liberty build and the third Quarkus 4.0 beta.
  • Inside Java on packing a ticker symbol into one int with a Valhalla value class.

AWS

  • AWS introduced Nitro Sandboxes on EKS, ECS and EC2 — hardware-isolated lightweight VMs, useful for sandboxing AI agents.
  • AWS Sign-In now supports OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange (RFC 8693), letting apps trade third-party OIDC tokens for AWS-scoped credentials.
  • CloudWatch Logs gained account-level retention policies for setting retention across log groups from one place.
  • AWS Glue added 100 new native connectors for SaaS and REST API sources.
  • DeepL wrote up how it keeps closest-exit routing during maintenance with AWS Cloud WAN and AS_PATH prepending.
  • Topstep's migration from self-managed Redis to ElastiCache for Valkey moved 53 million keys with a blue/green cutover and no app code changes.

AI and agents

  • Simon Willison had Claude Code track down a mysterious beep in a box room full of unpacked boxes.
  • Latent Space's deep dive into Handshake AI looks at what frontier labs buy for specialized training data.

Security

  • CISA added four actively-exploited flaws (OpenSSH, GPUStack, FreeSWITCH, IBM Aspera Faspex) to its KEV catalog.
  • Attackers compromised Ethersphere's own release pipeline to ship malicious bee-js and Swarm Desktop updates that steal wallet keys.
  • A lone attacker reportedly used AI agents to pull Taipei emergency dispatch records, including an exposed fire-department platform with patient data.
  • Schneier recaps the [un]prompted AI security conference and a framework for dividing AI security into three broad topics.

item.title: Digest for 2026-11-09
item.description:
Your stack

  • Python 3.14: Real Python dug into how CPython manages memory (arenas, pools, blocks) and its podcast covered free-threaded Python and the CPython ABI — useful background while free-threading keeps rolling out.
  • Linters and type checkers: Astral shipped ty 0.0.99, another point release of the Rust-based type checker.
  • FastAPI: FastAPI 0.162.2 shipped (and 0.162.1 just before it).
  • boto3: boto3 1.43.126 shipped.
  • Amazon Bedrock: Kimi K3.1 Pro (Highspeed) landed on Bedrock as a new open-weight model option. AWS also posted a two-part guide to governing AI agent access with Okta Cross App Access and AgentCore (part 2), binding agent identity to end users via Cedar policies — relevant if you're building agent authn/authz. Case studies from Greenlight Financial's autonomous SOC and Taxbit Assist show AgentCore in production, and AWS Agent Registry went GA in GovCloud (US-West).
  • GitHub Actions: Platform Engineering's "Beyond SHA pinning" argues pinned SHAs don't guarantee provenance and walks through how imposter commits exploit CI/CD workflows — worth a read for your supply-chain posture.
  • Checkmarx: Checkmarx joined the Claude Marketplace, letting Anthropic customers put spend toward Checkmarx Fusion SAST, Triage and Remediation Assist.
  • MCP: Spring AI 2.1.0-RC2 adds server support for the new MCP protocol revision. Microsoft's Work IQ API is getting SharePoint MCP tools for custom apps and agents, and AWS posted a walkthrough of a serverless MCP server on ECS Fargate for data-lake access.
  • Claude: researchers showed malicious browser extensions could abuse Claude Dispatch to run code on a user's computer via claude.ai — worth knowing if you run Claude Desktop with browser extensions installed.
  • Claude Code: two security stories worth your attention: Claude Code's "Don't Ask Again" file is exposing passwords and keys in 1,122 public GitHub repos (check your own repos for a committed settings file), and a fake Claude Code extension that tried to open a backdoor. On the feature side, 2.1.319 adds background MCP task support in the terminal, claude-agent-sdk 0.2.179 shipped, and AWS published a guide to running Claude Code as a remote AgentCore session with per-task isolation.
  • AI-DLC and AI-assisted development practices: GitHub Copilot got a flurry of updates — code review settings via API, and JetBrains Air/Xcode support plus an Agent Merge mode — alongside a GitHub blog post on what agentic engineering still needs human judgment for. Simon Willison suggests hiding noisy agent-generated PR descriptions behind <details><summary> if you're shipping a lot of Claude Code or Codex PRs. Elsewhere, Stanford's AI-native engineering course brought open-source maintainers in to grade student work, and Daniel Miessler argues real vibe coding isn't just "using AI to make things."
  • Security (AI and cloud): InfoQ on identity as an architectural concern argues IAM design choices drive your data models and service boundaries, not just authentication.

Python

  • Real Python on managing multiple Python versions with pyenv.
  • Real Python's introduction to Python SQL libraries.
  • Real Python on absolute vs. relative imports.

React

  • This week's React Status roundup highlights Redux Toolkit's road to 3.0.

Rust

  • Tokio-tun goes multi-platform (FreeBSD, macOS, iOS, Android) with Linux GSO/GRO offload, heading toward 1.0.
  • Neuro, a new compiled language for AI with a compiler written in Rust.
  • Logjar 0.1 lets you grep compressed log archives without decompressing them.

Go

  • The Go team explains Go's new JSON API.

Java

  • Inside Java on Java and the next generation of programming models, from Devoxx Belgium.
  • Spring Boot 4.2.0-RC2 is available from Maven Central.

IaC and DevOps

  • AWS Device Farm now lets you run Maestro tests on real Android devices.

Source control and GitHub

  • GitHub's Copilot impact dashboard now tracks chat and VS Code agent usage.
  • @GitHub in Slack and Teams is now generally available, letting you investigate bugs and open PRs without leaving the conversation.

AWS

  • SageMaker Inference now supports Multi-Instance GPU to improve GPU utilization on model endpoints.
  • AWS on a taxonomy of agentic primitives in Amazon Quick.
  • AWS Elemental MediaConvert adds AI-powered Smart Subtitles.
  • AWS Glue Data Catalog now supports catalog-vended credentials for Apache Iceberg REST federation.
  • Amazon Redshift's SUPER type now stores strings up to 16MB.
  • EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML now support amortization.

AI and agents

  • Simon Willison's parse_number() as a SQLite extension: C vs Rust, built with help from Claude.
  • Via Hacker News: AI is destroying my CS degree.
  • Latent Space talks biology with Fabian Theis of Helmholtz Munich.

Security

  • AWS on addressing protocol security gaps in multi-tenant Kubernetes (ADB, WebRTC and other unencrypted-by-default protocols).
  • CVE-2026-122193: OS command injection in example SSM documents in AWS's Trusted Remote Execution setup guide.
  • Trail of Bits: after Binance, check what your signing systems can approve.
  • CISA flagged a SonicWall SonicOS MFA bypass flaw under possible active exploitation.
  • Attackers are targeting the OpenSSH "SSHole" flaw within hours of disclosure, gaining root on a honeypot.
  • A Chainalysis breach exposed all users' credentials, forcing a shutdown of key services.

AI security

  • Daniel Miessler on the Bitter Lesson, generalized.

Python

JavaScript and TypeScript

AI and agents

Engineering practice

CISA advisories.

item.title: Digest for 2026-11-05
item.description:
Your stack

  • Linters and type checkers: Astral's ty 0.0.97 shipped (no changelog beyond the version bump).
  • boto3: boto3 1.43.124 shipped (no changelog beyond the version bump).
  • Amazon Bedrock: Bedrock added OpenAI GPT-5.6 (Terra/Luna) on bedrock-runtime plus Cross-Region Inference in AWS GovCloud (US); one post shows how to wire decision models (Jev, Strands Decider) into AgentCore Evaluations to validate a check before gating a release on it; another lays out a four-layer context-engineering framework for production agents, implemented in the open-source Deep Insight on Strands/AgentCore; and U Mobile's AgentCore-based telco ops platform now handles 150+ scenarios and has cut trouble tickets up to 84.5%.
  • Microsoft Teams: The GitHub app in Microsoft Teams is now GA, with a GitHub Canvas for reviewing and filing work without leaving Teams.
  • Claude: anthropic 2.5.0 (the Python SDK) shipped; separately, the two Bedrock AgentCore posts above build on Strands, the model-driven agent framework commonly paired with Claude on Bedrock.
  • AI-DLC and AI-assisted development practices: GitHub Copilot is now available in Xcode's built-in coding assistant (public preview); separately, Kiro's web search landed in AWS GovCloud (US), with admin controls to turn it off org-wide or per custom agent.
  • Entra ID: AWS DataSync Enhanced mode now authenticates to Google Cloud Storage and Azure Blob Storage via OIDC, pulling short-lived credentials from Microsoft Entra ID instead of long-term HMAC/SAS keys.
  • Security (AI and cloud): two new AWS bulletins: CVE-2026-122266, an eBPF connection-tracking isolation bug in the EKS Network Policy Agent that could let an adjacent pod bypass NetworkPolicy enforcement, and CVE-2026-122192, letting a guest root user read/modify the Firecracker host process's memory after a failed memory discard on snapshot-restored VMs. Separately, Check Point found "prompt adware" (Haiou) hidden in an OpenAI Codex jailbreak toolkit that rewrites the agent's trusted config to inject ads, and Sekoia traced an APT29 watering-hole campaign to a compromised web-analytics supply chain (Plerdy SEO Tracker) targeting iOS/Android. CISA and vendors also logged several more exploited or unpatched flaws this week: a patched Apple info-stealer flaw, a critical Android zero-click RCE, a WordPress Core TOCTOU bug, unpatched EoL SonicWall GMS flaws, and chainable Barracuda auth-bypass-plus-root-access flaws.

Python

  • Real Python on Positron IDE: a hands-on tutorial for cleaning, visualizing and exploring data manually or with AI assistance.
  • The PSF welcomed Joshua Mcshannon as its new Infrastructure Engineer, focused on cutting operational toil on PSF infrastructure.

JavaScript and TypeScript

  • Node.js has scheduled security releases for November 11.
  • A Node 27 alpha landed, the first release under Node's new six-months-in-alpha process.

Rust

  • xsd-parser v1.6.0 adds proper dynamic/abstract XSD type support and opt-in skipping of unknown elements.
  • PlanetX Lite 0.22.0, a Rust/wgpu 3D globe viewer, adds GIS vector layers (GeoPackage, Shapefile, GeoJSON and more).

Go

  • Go 1.27 introduces a new encoding/json/v2 and encoding/json/jsontext API.

Java

  • Project Detroit uses Java's Foreign Function & Memory API to embed whole foreign-language runtimes, like V8 and CPython, directly in Java apps instead of reimplementing them.

Source control and GitHub

  • CodeQL 2.27.4 improves query accuracy and metadata for GitHub code scanning.

Microsoft (Azure DevOps, Teams, WSL)

  • Intelligent Terminal 0.3 adds a sidebar for managing tabs and agent sessions, plus global search.
  • Microsoft is deprecating low-trust SharePoint add-ins in SharePoint Server Subscription Edition from January 12, 2027 — migrate to SPFx.

AWS

  • S3 Tables now manages migrating Apache Hive tables to Iceberg — no pipeline to build, production workloads keep running.
  • EC2 Capacity Manager adds real-time supportability checks and capacity-fulfillment metrics across instance types and AZs.

item.title: Digest for 2026-10-02
item.description:
Your stack

Amazon Bedrock

  • Building ambient agents with Bedrock AgentCore shows a framework-agnostic pattern for event-driven agents (SQS, Lambda, DynamoDB) with a human-in-the-loop ask_human tool — a solid reference if you're wiring agents to react to events instead of chat prompts.
  • AWS Professional Services used AgentCore to automate enterprise cloud migrations end to end, including IaC generation — a bigger data point for agentic IaC workflows.

Claude

  • Implementing multi-environment access for Claude Platform on AWS covers cross-account SigV4, workspace-scoped API keys and OIDC federation for external environments — directly useful if you run Claude from more than one AWS account.

MCP

  • CVE-2026-97662: argument injection in AWS's own security-agent-mcp-server diff scan — worth checking if you run that tool, and a reminder to treat MCP server inputs as untrusted.

Powertools for AWS Lambda

  • CVE-2026-104002: the data masking utility in Powertools for AWS Lambda (Python) fails open on errors instead of masking — update if you rely on it for PII redaction in logs.

DynamoDB

  • DynamoDB now supports filtered export to S3, so you can export a subset of a table instead of the whole thing.
  • DAX is now available in 17 more Regions.

GitHub Actions

  • macOS 14 runner images are being retired — move pinned workflows to macOS 15 before the cutoff.
  • Actions retention settings now cover checks, runs and statuses, not just logs and artifacts.

AWS Organizations and Control Tower

  • IAM Identity Center now replicates to more opt-in Regions, including GovCloud and China.
  • GuardDuty now supports AWS Organizations declarative policies for centrally enabling threat detection org-wide.

boto3

  • boto3 1.43.107 is out — routine SDK bump.

Security (AI and cloud)

  • GitHub shipped rate limits and structured forms for private vulnerability reports, tightening up the coordinated-disclosure flow on repos.
  • AWS Secrets Manager's console now gives actionable security posture recommendations per secret.
  • AWS Security Hub now groups related exposures into remediation plans by root cause instead of one finding at a time.
  • AWS Continuum for Penetration Testing expanded to 6 more Regions.
  • A critical FortiMail zero-day is under active exploitation and allows unauthenticated arbitrary file writes — patch if you run FortiMail.

Python

  • PEP 818 (Pyodide FFI core for Python) is back up for discussion after a round of trims and renames.

IaC and DevOps

  • GitHub Copilot can now interact with desktop apps via computer use, in public preview on macOS and Windows.
  • VS Code's September Copilot releases add automations for repeatable tasks and agent-assisted PR merges.
  • Code coverage uploads no longer fail CI on branches without an open PR yet.
  • Scheduled code scanning now skips inactive repos, only running after real pushes or PRs.

AWS

  • AWS Well-Architected Agent is in preview — an AI service that reviews your environment and proposes ready-to-apply fixes across cost, security, performance and resilience.
  • GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring is now bundled into the Security Hub Threat Analytics plan.
  • Route 53 Global Resolver and DNS Firewall gained native CloudWatch DNS analytics.
  • Systems Manager documents can now be shared org-wide via AWS RAM instead of per-account.

Security

  • A self-healing WordPress backdoor persists across files, the database and shared memory, re-infecting the site after cleanup.
  • This week's tl;dr sec roundup covers Google's PageBreak web app scanner and Perplexity's agent-security tooling.

AI security

  • Daniel Miessler argues AI agents should pay the people whose work they draw on, a provocation worth a read as agentic workflows scale up.

Engineering practice

  • The Pragmatic Engineer on Firebase's global outage and weak incident response, plus notes on OpenAI's AWS-like platform ambitions.
  • Stripe explains why it tried to kill token-based billing and kept it anyway — a useful read if you price an API or agent product by usage.

Feeds that failed

CISA advisories (malformed XML).
